sections.title: Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 arrive on AWS
paragraphs: Anthropic announced Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2 on 9 November 2026 and made them available through Amazon Bedrock and the Claude Platform on AWS[S1][S2]. The two models are positioned as the most capable generally available versions for technical work, with Fable aimed at coding, math and science and Mythos targeting high‑risk domains such as cyber security and life sciences[S1][S2].

Fable 5.2 is described as able to handle ambiguous, multi‑step tasks, verify its own output and run unattended for hours to days, while also catching errors and optimizing as it proceeds[S1]. In internal testing the model solved two open theoretical‑physics problems, helped engineers complete large software migrations, and formalized a proof of Fermat’s Last Theorem in 30 hours[S2]. Pricing was lowered from $10 to $8 per million input tokens, making it cheaper than GPT‑6 Astra, and the model returns responses about 30 % faster across effort levels, with an optional faster inference tier at double price[S3].

The new models build on earlier versions (Fable 5.1, Mythos 5.1) and incorporate the Enterprise Frontier Safeguards system that supports zero‑data‑retention compliance[S1][S3]. They also continue Anthropic’s alignment testing, which claims reduced hallucinations and more reliable task completion compared with prior models such as Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5[S1].

sections.title: Gemini pulls personal Drive and email data for review
paragraphs: Google Gemini now routes personal Gmail, Docs, and Drive content to human reviewers when Connected Apps are enabled[S4]. The change was announced in an October 16 edit to the 2023 Gemini Workspace blog post and confirmed in Google Help Answer 16836988[S4]. The routing happens automatically during chat, even without explicit @Drive or @Gmail tags, and the retrieval is probabilistic[S4].

When a user mentions personal topics such as trips, bills, or reservations, Gemini may trigger a background Workspace lookup[S4]. The system can produce four outcomes: no retrieval, a generic summary, a partial unredacted excerpt of 2–4 sentences, or full ingestion of the entire document or email[S4]. Tests show that the same query can yield different outcomes on repeated runs because the tool‑calling step is nondeterministic[S4].

Google originally promised in 2023 that personal content would not be seen by human reviewers[S4]. The recent policy reversal means that any data accessed through Connected Apps can be sent to human review pipelines, raising privacy concerns for users who assume their files remain private[S4]. Understanding that the retrieval is probabilistic helps explain why some users may not see data extraction in a single test, but the pipeline still exists[S4].

sections.title: The race is on to sue Nvidia
paragraphs: Nvidia's shares fell more than 4% on Monday, the first trading day after its board announced an investigation into CEO Jensen Huang's relationship with Alice Huang, a former Megaspeed executive suspected of spying for China[S5]. A Los Angeles shareholder‑rights firm, Schall, Brown & Schwartz, said It is probing whether Nvidia gave false or misleading statements to investors[S5]. Stanford law professor Robert Bartlett expects a securities filing to appear by the end of the day[S5].

The investigation follows a New York Times report that linked Jensen Huang to Alice Huang, who U.S. intelligence monitored for over a year[S5]. Nvidia previously described the relationship as "not unusual or unexpected" and said meetings with customers are part of a CEO's job[S5]. Bartlett characterises the earlier company statement as clearly misleading and notes that, because Huang is CEO, his knowledge is imputed to Nvidia, supporting a classic fraud‑on‑the‑market claim[S5].

Under federal securities law, the first complaint triggers a public notice and gives investors 60 days to request lead plaintiff status, giving early filers a strategic advantage[S5]. Lawsuits of this type aim to recover losses when investors claim they paid inflated prices based on false disclosures[S5]. Nvidia is headquartered in Santa Clara, so any case will likely be filed in the Northern District of California[S5].

sections.title: Meta expands Instagram AI age‑guessing globally
paragraphs: Meta announced on 9 November 2026 that It is expanding its AI‑powered age‑estimation technology on Instagram worldwide to identify more teens and place them under Teen Account protections[S6][S7]. The company also said it will extend the same system to Facebook now and to Threads later this year[S6][S7].

The AI scans entire profiles for contextual clues such as birthday celebrations, school grades, and visual cues like height or bone structure[S6][S7]. It examines posts, comments, bios, captions, photos and videos to estimate age[S6][S7]. Users judged to be 13‑17 are moved into teen accounts even if they entered an adult birthdate[S6][S7].

The rollout follows Meta’s settlement of up to $18 billion with nearly every U.S. state and territory in August 2026 over lawsuits alleging its platforms harm teens[S6][S7]. The settlement required stronger teen identification, prompting the global expansion[S6][S7].

sections.title: Korea secures AI agents with NVIDIA OpenShell
paragraphs: NVIDIA announced that its Open Agent Safety Platform, including the OpenShell runtime, is being used by Korean firms to protect AI agents handling enterprise tasks[S8].

OpenShell offers sandboxed execution and policy‑based controls that limit data exposure and manage tool access for autonomous agents[S8]. AIM Intelligence plans a proof‑of‑concept for the public energy sector, aiming to detect malicious instructions and prevent data leakage using Starfort’s detection capabilities together with OpenShell’s access controls[S8]. Meanwhile, NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang disclosed a personal affair that triggered an independent board investigation due to concerns about foreign intelligence targeting the company[S9].
AI agents are increasingly deployed for tasks such as employee productivity and industrial automation, which raises concerns about data security and unauthorized actions[S8].

why_it_matters.text: Investors may see further price volatility and could file lawsuits to recover losses if the probe confirms that Nvidia provided false information, affecting retirement accounts and corporate portfolios that hold the stock[S5].
